paper_metadata.title: Phase-Field Study of Anisotropic g0-Coarsening Kinetics in Ni-Base Superalloys with Varying Re and Ru Contents

evidence.quote: The typical microstructure of single crystalline Ni-base cast alloys consists of cuboidal g0-precipitates coherently embedded in a continuous g-matrix (Ni). The extraordinary thermo-mechanical properties of the Ni-base superalloys largely depend on the morphology, distribution, size, and volume fraction of the g0-precipitates.
The coarsening kinetics of g0-precipitates in single crystalline Ni-based superalloys were studied using phase-field simulations
We first determine the exponents for coarsening without elastic effects in Ni–9.6 wt%Al denoted as NiAl(NE)

Since the diffusive transport of material away from or toward the interface is rather slow but still a necessary requirement for the overall process to evolve, the kinetics of coarsening is said to be diffusion-limited.
The respective driving force is called the Gibbs-Thompson effect or capillarity.
